builder_plan.scenario: Your coding assistant makes changes that still need substantial repair before merging.
builder_plan.change: Try the technique on held-out issues from a repository with reliable tests.
builder_plan.baseline: The same coding agent, repository snapshot, tools, and token budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct patches, regression failures, human repair time, and total cost per accepted change.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Solve Vision with Code: Coding Agents Are Stronger Visual Reasoners Than Video Models
summary: Replaces prompt-conditioned video generation models, where reasoning unfolds in denoised pixels, with a coding agent that receives the same first frame and prompt and writes a program that renders the answer video for an unmodified rule-based evaluator. Cost is LLM API spend per instance (or an open-weight model within the 24 GB budget at substantially lower accuracy, 0.572 versus 0.923) plus one rendering execution, with no GPU training or video-model serving required. It can fail on tasks whose solutions are not computable from a first frame and prompt alone, it depends on a rule-based evaluator with symbolic ground truth so gains may not transfer to open-ended visual tasks, and propositional programs that hard-code values may not generalize beyond the benchmark distribution.
rationale: The method uses API-accessible coding agents plus deterministic rendering, fits a 24 GB / API-only budget, and the reported accuracy margin over video models is large enough that visual-reasoning pipelines built on video generation are currently the weaker default.

claims.statement: Replaces prompt-conditioned video generation models, where reasoning unfolds in denoised pixels, with a coding agent that receives the same first frame and prompt and writes a program that renders the answer video for an unmodified rule-based evaluator. Cost is LLM API spend per instance (or an open-weight model within the 24 GB budget at substantially lower accuracy, 0.572 versus 0.923) plus one rendering execution, with no GPU training or video-model serving required. It can fail on tasks whose solutions are not computable from a first frame and prompt alone, it depends on a rule-based evaluator with symbolic ground truth so gains may not transfer to open-ended visual tasks, and propositional programs that hard-code values may not generalize beyond the benchmark distribution.

Three closed-model coding agents score 0.923, 0.894 and 0.893 on VBVR-Pro-Bench, each more than 0.22 accuracy points above the strongest video generation model; the best open-weight agent (GLM-5) reaches 0.572.
